primarySources.finding: Official Bazel docs explicitly describe macOS sandbox-exec nesting as unsupported. This supports an outer Seatbelt conflict; it is not a trace of our installed Chrome.
Chromium native implementation calls sandbox_init / sandbox_init_with_parameters and sandbox_apply for its own policies.
Child startup receives the serialized policy and initializes its native sandbox.
Deserialized policy is applied through Seatbelt compiled or source initialization; failure returns false.

Default DIR_CRASH_DUMPS is based on default user data directory and appends Crashpad on macOS; it deliberately does not follow a later --user-data-dir override. Therefore an isolated profile alone is insufficient for Crashpad location.

Create reads BREAKPAD_DUMP_LOCATION and, when nonempty, overrides DIR_CRASH_DUMPS. GetCrashDumpLocation returns that overridden key. This is a source-supported owned crash path mechanism without changing HOME or disabling sandbox.
On POSIX Create runs before macOS InitMacCrashReporter, supporting that override ordering.
The macOS initial Crashpad handler receives GetCrashDumpLocation as its database path.

inference: b2 actual reached a CDP port, WebSocket connected then disconnected; native initializationEPERM repeats, GPUexit6 loops, GPUunusableFATAL and actualSIGTRAP. With known parent sandbox-exec inheritance, native nested Seatbelt conflict is the leading supported explanation, not simply a missing file-write directory.

Do not fix this by increasing connect timeout, repeatedly allowing personal Crashpad paths, disabling Chrome sandbox/GPU sandbox, adding --no-sandbox, or attributing disk collapse to this run. Exact installed154 source/syscall chain still unconfirmed.
MAC temporary-path repair improved progress beyond the first ProcessSingleton stage, but a successful native temp creation is not actual UI success.
